text:
Workers' share of the economy just hit the lowest level ever recorded.

BLS has tracked this since 1947. It has never been lower than it is right now.
why_now: New BLS productivity release (Q3 2026) shows labor share at a record low.

text:
Electricity prices are up 43% since January 2021. Prices overall are up 28.5%.

Lower-income families spend a much bigger share of their budget on utilities, so they feel this first. With data centers pulling more power every month, I don't see it slowing down.
why_now: Oct CPI; winter utility bills; data-center power demand in the news.

text:
California just voted down a billionaire tax after tech spent $425 million to kill it.

Worth remembering where new billionaires come from. 64% of the ones minted last year came from states where Democrats control both the governor's office and the legislature.

Blue states are great at making billionaires. Taxing them is another story.
why_now: Prop 40 failed Nov 10 after record tech spending.

text:
The USDA wants to cut 6.3 million more people off SNAP. They announced it two weeks before Thanksgiving.

Food banks were already saying demand is up this year. This makes it a lot worse.
why_now: USDA proposed SNAP rule (Nov 10); Thanksgiving week coming.

text:
The top 1% now own 32.5% of all the wealth in America. A record.

The entire bottom half of the country owns 2.3%.

1% of households have 14 times the wealth of 50% of households.
why_now: Fed DFA Q2 2026 shows record top-1% share.

text:
Americans now owe a record $1.1 trillion on their credit cards. The average interest rate is 21%.

Carrying a balance at 21% is one of the most expensive ways to be broke in America.
why_now: Fed H.8 weekly data (Nov 4) shows a new record; Fed hike expected in December.

text:
New York is now the most unequal state in America, per new Census data. Then DC, Connecticut, Louisiana and California.

The most equal state? Utah.

A lot of deep blue on the unequal end of this map. Something to sit with now that Democrats run Congress.
why_now: ACS 2025 1-year estimates just released.

text:
In Louisiana, 25% of kids live below the poverty line, with Mississippi and DC right behind at nearly the same rate.

Nationally it's 14.8%, in the richest country in the world.
why_now: ACS 2025 1-year estimates.

text:
Democrats just won the House and the Senate. Here's where I'd start.

The federal minimum wage has been $7.25 since July 2009. After inflation, it's now worth less than at any point since 1949.

In 1968 it was worth $15.79 in today's dollars.
why_now: New Democratic Congress; Oct CPI release.

text:
Black unemployment was 6.6% in October, compared with 3.7% for white workers.

This chart goes back to 1972, through booms, recessions and recoveries, and the gap has barely moved.
why_now: October jobs report (Nov 6).

text:
A child who grows up in a low-income family in Shelby County, Tennessee, reaches the 32nd income percentile as an adult. A child from the same family income in Bergen County, New Jersey, reaches the 52nd.

Same starting point, and a very different life depending on the county where it begins.
why_now: Replaces reused homelessness chart; Opportunity Atlas county map (new).

text:
Since 2022, Microsoft's revenue has grown 67% while its workforce has grown 1%, in this chart from @[Steve Rattner](1658881).

This is what it looks like when the gains from AI flow to shareholders instead of workers, and it lines up with the record low labor share from earlier this week.
why_now: Reshare: Rattner note (Nov 13) spreading fast; ties to Monday's labor-share note.

text:
The typical first-time homebuyer in America is now 40 years old. In 1981 it was 29.

And a record share of first-time buyers paid all cash this year. That money isn't coming from paychecks. It's coming from parents.
why_now: NAR Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers (Nov 5).

text:
In Hawaii, the typical home costs 8.6 times the typical household's income. In California it's 7.5 times, while in West Virginia it's 2.9.

The old rule of thumb was that a home should cost about 3 years of income, and most of the country left that behind a long time ago.
why_now: Follows the NAR first-time buyer news; ACS 2025.

text:
Pedestrians in New Mexico are 5x more likely to be killed by a car than pedestrians in Iowa, and it's getting worse. Great map from @[Aziz Sunderji](2432780).

Walking is how a lot of lower-income Americans get to work, and in too many states it's a dangerous way to get there.
why_now: Reshare: Aziz Sunderji map (Nov 11); Jeremy's car-safety notes perform well.
source_kind: reshare: Aziz Sunderji / The Pro Map

text:
Rents in San Francisco are up 26% in a single year, the fastest of any large county in America, as AI money pours into the Bay Area. The typical large county saw rents rise 2.5%.

The teachers, nurses and bus drivers who keep the city running aren't getting AI-sized raises.
why_now: Replaces reused insurance map; Zillow ZORI through Oct 2026.

text: Corporate profits are now a bigger share of the economy than at any point on record at the same time that workers' share of those gains just hit a record low.
why_now: BEA Q2 data; callback to Monday's labor share note.

text: Since 2006, rent is up 103%. Hourly pay is up 90%.That gap might not sound huge, but for any family trying to put a roof over their head it can be the difference between a secure household and living in a shelter.
why_now: Weekend evening; Oct CPI and jobs data.

text: In the early 1950s, corporate income taxes made up about a third of federal tax revenue. Today it's 14%.
why_now: Prop 40 aftermath; BEA Q2 data.

text: Wholesale prices are up 6.5% from a year ago, the fastest pace since 2022. That's what businesses pay to stock the shelves, which is going to impact your holiday spending. Those higher prices show up for families right around the holidays.
why_now: PPI release (Nov 13); Fed signaling a December hike.

text: Some actual good news: real median household income hit a record $87,460 in 2025. But we need to view the median next to the wealth of those at the very top, which also hit a record this week. it The top 1% hold 32.5% of all wealth.
why_now: Census income data; balances the record-inequality notes earlier in the week.

text:
4.6 million kids in America have no health insurance. In Texas it's 1 in 8.

Most uninsured kids already qualify for Medicaid or CHIP. Their families just aren't enrolled. Open enrollment just started and runs through January 15.
why_now: 2027 ACA open enrollment; ACS 2025 shows uninsured kids rising in 32 states.

text:
Half of all renters in America are now cost burdened. 22.5 million households, per new Census data.

When you look at old HUD documents you see things about this being their crisis scenario, but now it is the US baseline.
why_now: ACS 2025 1-year estimates.

text:
2021 monthly payment for a new home: $1,285
Today: $2,117

$830 more every month, and prices barely came down.
why_now: Mortgage rates back above 7%; Fed hike expected.

text:
Two days before Thanksgiving, here's who relies on SNAP right now.

15.4 million households got food assistance in 2025. In New Mexico it's nearly 1 in 5. In Oregon, West Virginia and New York, about 1 in 6.

The USDA wants to cut 6.3 million people from the program.
why_now: Thanksgiving week; USDA proposed SNAP rule (Nov 10).

text:
Public schools counted 1.5 million homeless students. HUD's count of homeless kids was about 134,000.

That 11x gap exists because HUD doesn't count families doubled up with relatives or sleeping on a friend's couch, and schools do. How a problem gets defined decides how big it looks.
why_now: HUD's 'record drop' announcement; follow-up to Thursday's note.

text:
The biggest rent increases last year weren't in New York or California.

Rents in New Hampshire jumped 11.8%, followed by Maine and South Carolina at nearly 10%, then the Dakotas and Wyoming. The national average was 4.7%. When everyone moves somewhere cheap, it stops being cheap.
why_now: ACS 2025 vs 2024; Realtor.com rent-hike coverage (Nov 12).

text:
Driving to your family for Thanksgiving? Gas is averaging $4.00 a gallon. A year ago it was $3.06.

That's a 31% jump, and it hits hardest for people who can't work from home.
why_now: Thanksgiving travel day; EIA weekly prices.

text:
The Farm Bureau says Thanksgiving dinner got slightly cheaper this year. Good.

Groceries overall still cost 28% more than they did in January 2021. That's the number families are actually living with.
why_now: Farm Bureau Thanksgiving survey (Nov 9); Oct CPI.

text:
91% of affluent households gave to charity a decade ago. In 2024 it was 81%.

For everyone else it fell from 56% to 41%. That part isn't stinginess. Rent and groceries come first.
why_now: Thanksgiving / Giving Tuesday run-up.

text:
Happy Thanksgiving. It's also Native American Heritage Month.

18.1% of American Indian and Alaska Native people live below the poverty line, per new Census data, compared with 19.9% of Black Americans and 9.4% of white Americans.
why_now: Thanksgiving + Native American Heritage Month; ACS 2025.

text:
Millions of Americans will eat out today, and the federal minimum wage for the people serving them is $2.13 an hour.

It hasn't changed since 1991.
why_now: Thanksgiving restaurant traffic.

text:
Since January 2020, the typical home in New Hampshire has gained 75% in value, with Connecticut and Maine close behind. In DC, home values are slightly down.

For families who owned before 2020, that's a windfall sitting at the Thanksgiving table. For their kids trying to buy, it's the bar they now have to clear.
why_now: Replaces repeated labor-share chart; Thanksgiving night; Zillow ZHVI Oct 2026.

text:
Americans are saving 3.8% of their income, the lowest since 2022.

Expect record Black Friday headlines anyway. A lot of that spending comes from the top. For most families, the cushion is getting thin.
why_now: Black Friday; BEA personal income release.

text:
Property insurers collected $1.03 trillion in premiums last year. The most ever, and more than the entire US military budget.

Meanwhile the five biggest home insurers didn't pay out on 44% of claims.
why_now: Evergreen insurance stat.

text:
There are now 242 cities in America where a typical starter home costs $1 million or more.

A starter home.
why_now: Zillow/Fortune report (Nov 7).

text:
Black kids who grow up in low-income families reach the 32nd income percentile as adults, on average. White kids from families with the same income reach the 45th.

Family income explains a lot about where kids end up, but it clearly doesn't explain all of it.
why_now: Replaces top-1% ladder that repeated Nov 17's wealth data; Opportunity Atlas.

text:
Adults without a high school diploma have a 4.9% unemployment rate, nearly double the 2.6% for people with a bachelor's degree.

That gap has been there for as long as this data has existed.
why_now: October jobs report.

text:
Per-capita income in one DUMBO census tract is $163,000. Right next door in Vinegar Hill, it's $18,000.

Two neighborhoods a few blocks apart with a 9x gap. Incredible map from @[Aziz Sunderji](2432780).
why_now: Reshare: Aziz Sunderji Pro Map (Nov 13); neighborhood inequality, weekend evening.
source_kind: reshare: Aziz Sunderji / The Pro Map

text:
$84 trillion is going to pass from older Americans to their heirs by 2045. The biggest wealth transfer in history.

It's mostly going to the people who already had a head start.
why_now: Holiday weekend family/estate conversations.

text:
Since 1973, American workers have become 163% more productive, but their real pay per hour is up just 64%.

Corporate profits and the top 1%'s share of wealth both just hit record highs. That's where the rest went.
why_now: Wrap-up of the month's labor-share thread.

text:
Back to work tomorrow, so one more from the new Census data.

Renters in Florida spend a median 35.5% of their income on rent, compared with 23.8% in North Dakota. Same country, very different math.

What should I map next?
why_now: Sunday evening reply-bait.
